judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward definitional provision naming the parties; the only defects are transcription artifacts (a comma for a period) that do not change meaning, and no term carries two reasonable readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the rest of the instrument, though the Lender is separately re-defined in Arbitration paragraph 1 as 'any Lender who provides you with a loan as a result of our services,' a slightly broader formulation than the named DSI Lending Resources.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The promised services are framed as attempts ('we will attempt to', 'we do not promise that you will actually receive a loan') and include vague items such as 'assist you in creating a positive credit history' and 'maintain a network of branch locations,' leaving what was actually bargained for open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It caps the lender's contract rate at ten percent while the Cost and Payment Terms (c004) recite a 708.90% CAB fee and a 713.38% APR, and it sits against the Disclosure of Fee as Finance Charge (c003) which says the fee 'is not interest' — a characterisation a usury claimant would contest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single sentence asserts a legal characterisation — that the CAB fee 'is not interest' — which is precisely the kind of label a court may have to construe against the substance of the charge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with c004, which computes the fee as an 'annualized rate' folded into a 713.38% APR and financed as part of the loan, and with c005's 'plus 10% per annum' reimbursement charge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbers do not add up on their face: $3.00 interest plus a $556.15 CAB fee is $559.15, not the stated $561.15 finance charge; the 'Total of Payments' is given as $86.15 when ten bi-weekly payments of $86.15 are scheduled; and the fee rate (708.90%) and APR (713.38%) diverge — classic mechanical error affecting meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recited 10.00% lender interest matches c002's cap but the total charge structure is in tension with c003's insistence that the fee is not interest, and the prorated refund promise interacts with the acceleration language in c007.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A late charge equal to the greater of 5% or $7.50' does not say 5% of what (the instalment, the balance, or the loan), and the run-on list of reimbursables ending in 'attorneys' fees, and costs of collection' has no stated limit of reasonableness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and partially overlaps the fee-shifting in c012 (which does add a reasonableness qualifier) and the reimbursement obligation in c006, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially garbled ('Chapter $ of the Texas Business and Commerce Code', a scrambled opening sentence) and the amount of the LOC is stated only as 'not to exceed principal, interest, returned item fee, and late fee, as applicable,' leaving the ceiling indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its savings language is a verbatim duplicate of the COMPLIANCE clause (c010) and of part of Arbitration paragraph 4 (c022), and its automatic revocation on timely cancellation must be read with the three-day cancellation notices (c033–c034), which use two different trigger dates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is badly mangled in its operative trigger clauses ('you do not pay us what you owe yr~ader this Agreement', 'fail to perform your obligations tot! ander'), so what counts as default — including whether default to the Lender is default to CAB — cannot be read off the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Acceleration of obligations 'less any unearned charges' has to be squared with the prorated CAB-fee refund promised in c004 and with the LOC presentment conditions in c006, which allow the lender to draw only after ten days of default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional waiver list, but the catch-all cast of 'you, and others responsible' and the blanket waiver of notice 'except for notices provided in this Agreement' is boilerplate rather than genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' and that 'we may sue or arbitrate with one or more persons without joining others' sits awkwardly against the Arbitration Provision (c021, c024), which makes binding arbitration the exclusive route for all disputes outside small claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It waives jury trial 'in the event of litigation' while cross-referring to a differently named instrument, the 'Jury Trial Waiver and Arbitration Agreement,' and conditions itself on the customer not 'reject[ing]' that agreement — a term used nowhere else.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitration section is actually titled 'Waiver of Jury Trial and Arbitration Provision' and provides an 'opt-out' process (c027), not a rejection, and c019 says no court other than small claims will resolve disputes at all, so the relationship between this standalone waiver and the arbitration clause is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard usury savings clause; its terms ('lawful amounts', 'maximum lawful rate') take their content from statute rather than from contested contract wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated nearly verbatim in c006 and inside Arbitration paragraph 4 (c022), which is redundant but not inconsistent with anything else in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any claim that this agreement or related matter, or any action or inaction by us or Lender, or by any other person, is legally non-compliant' is a sweeping catch-all, and 'any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability' does not say what corrective action suffices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As a condition precedent to suit it must be reconciled with the arbitration paragraph 4 requirement of 30 days' notice to remedy circumstances precluding arbitration (c022) and with the small-claims right preserved in c024.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable attorneys' fees ... and all costs and disbursements' is ordinary fee-shifting language, though the appended statutory sentence about criminal charges is a non-sequitur bolted onto a fee clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the unqualified 'attorneys' fees, and costs of collection' in c005 — one says reasonable, the other does not — but the two can be harmonised in the customer's favour.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short stipulation with no ambiguous term; 'for all purposes' is broad but its function — supporting FAA coverage — is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns exactly with Arbitration paragraph 7 (c025) and the Governing Law clause (c028), which likewise invoke the FAA on an interstate-commerce footing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plainly one-sided (we may assign at discretion, you may not) but definite; nothing in the wording admits of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Arbitration paragraph 8 (c026), which binds and benefits the parties' successors and assigns.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure informational recitation of addresses and a phone number with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same Chicago address recurs in c011, c027 and c036, and the Texas service agent is consistent with the Texas governing law clause (c028).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Explanatory preamble rather than an operative term, though it states flatly that arbitrating parties 'waive their rights to file a lawsuit and proceed in court,' which overstates what follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That statement is qualified by the small-claims carve-out in c019 and c024 and by the court-resolution fallback in c021 and c026, so this introduction and the operative paragraphs do not describe the same regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives 'dispute' the 'broadest possible meaning' and then enumerates ten categories 'without limitation' — a textbook general-versus-specific problem — and expressly sweeps in 'the validity and scope of this Arbitration Provision,' a delegation formulation courts routinely have to construe; it also misdescribes the instrument as 'this Disclosure Statement.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The delegation of validity to the arbitrator collides with paragraph 3 (c021), which says the validity and enforceability of the class waiver shall be determined 'solely by a court of competent jurisdiction and not by the arbitrator.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalised acknowledgment of jury-trial waiver; the transcription is garbled but the substance ('giving up your right to have a trial by jury') is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the separate WAIVER OF RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY clause (c009), which purports to operate in litigation and is conditioned on not rejecting the arbitration agreement, creating a layering question but no flat contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in its terms: no court other than a small claims tribunal resolves disputes; the only defect is OCR noise in the party references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with c021 and c026, which both contemplate the dispute proceeding in court if the class-wide waiver is not enforced — a court route this clause says the customer has given up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear class and representative-action waiver in capitals; 'for any purpose(s)' is broad but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its blanket bar on consolidation is qualified by paragraph 6's small-claims right (c024) and by the court fallback in paragraph 3 (c021) and the blow-up clause in paragraph 8 (c026).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It reserves the validity of the class waiver 'solely' to a court while the surrounding provision delegates validity and scope questions broadly, and its 'if the arbitrator fails or refuses to abide ... and the court refuses to enforce' condition describes a sequence that is hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its remedy (the dispute proceeds in court) is inconsistent with paragraph 8 (c026), which says that if the class-arbitration bar is invalid the entire Arbitration Provision is void, and with paragraph 1's delegation of validity questions (c017).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The customer may pick 'any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us,' and forfeits the choice if no selection is made in 20 days, while the fee advance is capped at $1000 — the mix of open-ended discretion and a general catch-all after two named organisations invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $1000 advance cap conflicts with paragraph 5 (c023), which promises to advance the customer's whole portion of the arbitration expenses without any cap, and the embedded 30-day pre-arbitration cure duplicates the 60-day pre-suit notice in c011.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mostly determinate, though 'a decision or an award in your favor resolving the dispute' does not say whether partial relief counts, which drives who bears the Arbitration Fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its unlimited advance of the customer's arbitration expenses cannot be squared with paragraph 4's 'up to $1000' cap and its statement that the arbitrator decides who ultimately pays (c022).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Disputes within the scope of such tribunal's jurisdiction' and the direction that a small-claims appeal goes to arbitration are workable but leave the boundary between the two forums to be worked out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception in paragraph 3 (c021) and in c019, and its preservation of small-claims adjudication for class-barred claims sits alongside the consolidation bar in c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard FAA choice-of-law term with a fallback to Texas arbitration law; the trigger ('a final, non-appealable judgment ... finds ... that the FAA does not apply') is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Governing Law clause (c028) and the interstate-commerce stipulation (c013), so the FAA/Texas split is coherent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blow-up proviso — the whole Arbitration Provision is void if the class-arbitration bar is 'deemed invalid or unenforceable' — turns on who deems it so and when, and survival 'unless you and we otherwise agree in writing' is a further contingency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts paragraph 3 (c021), which contemplates the dispute simply proceeding in court if the class waiver is not enforced rather than voiding the entire provision, and it cuts against the general reformation/severability rule in the ENTIRE AGREEMENT clause (c031).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opt-out mechanics are materially garbled in the operative sentence (the notice address and the words 'notify us in writing within ninety (90) calendar days' are broken up), and it demands a social security number as a condition of a right whose exercise is otherwise simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A ninety-day opt-out is hard to reconcile with the signature-block certification that the customer agrees to 'the binding Waiver Of Jury Trial And Arbitration Provision' (c032) and with c009's reference to 'rejecting' the arbitration agreement, which uses different terminology for the same escape hatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: Texas law generally, FAA for the arbitration provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with paragraph 7 (c025), although paragraph 7 adds a Texas-arbitration-law fallback that this clause does not mention, a small gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-style warning in capitals with no operative obligation; 'short-term' and 'repeated or frequent use' are vague but nothing turns on them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with the one-day service period and short instalment schedule in c002 and c004 and imposes no duty that could conflict with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure contact information mandated by regulation, with no term capable of two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument bears on it; it does not compete with the pre-suit notice clause (c011), which concerns claims rather than complaints.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard integration plus a reformation/severability rule; 'reformed if practicable so as to achieve its intended purpose(s)' is somewhat open-ended but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its severability rule that invalidity 'shall not in any way affect the remaining provisions' is contradicted by paragraph 8 (c026), under which invalidity of the class-arbitration bar voids the whole Arbitration Provision, and the integration language sits against the separately referenced loan documents and cancellation notices (c032, c033).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment list is severely mangled where it identifies the documents received ('A SEPARATE ... THIS ZES AGREEMENT WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED'), so what the customer certified to having received cannot be determined from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its certification that the customer agrees to 'the binding Waiver Of Jury Trial And Arbitration Provision' pulls against the ninety-day opt-out in c027, and the warranty of no bankruptcy intention sits oddly with paragraph 8 (c026), which contemplates obligations discharged through bankruptcy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction' is definite in form, but 'the date of the transaction' is not defined and may or may not mean the signing date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Notice of Cancellation (c034) measures the same period from 'the date the contract is signed,' a different trigger, though both point to the 04/12/2012 deadline given in c036 for a 4/9/2012 execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple and clear: cancellation without penalty within three days after signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses a signing-date trigger where c033 uses 'the date of the transaction,' and its 'without any penalty or obligation' has to be squared with the LOC revocation and fee provisions in c006 and c004.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line refund promise; the only flaw is the missing space in 'within10 days,' which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with c006's automatic revocation of the LOC on timely cancellation and with c004's fee-refund mechanics; no competing provision addresses refunds on cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanically clear instructions with a fixed deadline; the duplicated company name is a formatting slip, not a change of meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stated 04/12/2012 deadline matches the three-day periods in c033 and c034 measured from the 4/9/2012 execution date, so the cancellation package is internally coherent.
